collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 4-10; in the story (name1) walks with two wooden crutches)

collection.description: A child guards the crutches of a villager who swims like a fish: thank the guard, or invite them swimming.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) walks with two crutches, and in the water (subject.he/she) doesn't need them at all: (subject.he/she) swims like a fish, far and fast and for hours. (subject.He/she) leaves the crutches propped on a rock by the shore. Today (friend) has appointed (friend.him/her)self official Guard of the Crutches and is standing beside them with a stick, glaring at anybody who walks past.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: When (subject) finally swims back in, (friend) reports that nobody touched the crutches, one crab tried, and the crab was sent away. (subject) thanks (friend.him/her) solemnly and asks if (friend.he/she) can be hired again tomorrow. (friend) says yes. The fee is one shell a day. (subject) pays it. The crab is never seen again.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) calls out to (friend) to come in. (friend) is torn: (friend.he/she) has a job to do. In the end (friend.he/she) drags the crutches higher up the beach, where the tide can't reach, puts a stone on them "so they don't run away," and splashes in. (subject) teaches (friend.him/her) to float on (friend.his/her) back. (friend) checks on the crutches every few minutes anyway.
